title: Atlas canonical entity record
description: One canonical domain-entity record. Status: accepted (S03 human review, 2026-09-30; D-022 to D-025). This file is the one home of field shapes and controlled-vocabulary values. Why each type exists, its identity test and what it must not be confused with are in docs/architecture/entity-taxonomy.md.

company.description: A legal person that can own, operate and contract. Business models are roles, not types (D-024). Ownership and operation of facilities are relationships (S04), not fields.

legal_name.description: Registered legal name, as a source states it.

incorporated_in.description: Jurisdiction of incorporation. Not the headquarters and not any facility location (S09 distinction).

headquartered_in.description: Jurisdiction of the headquarters, as a source states it. Not the incorporation and not any facility location.

roles.description: Business-model roles the company holds, each claim-backed and optionally time-bounded. Several at once are normal (blurs B-2, B-3).

facility.description: A physical site at a location where production or computing takes place. Who owns or operates it is a relationship (S04), never a field.

facility_kinds.description: What the site does. More than one kind is allowed, because one site can both fabricate wafers and package dies (blur B-3).

located_in.description: Jurisdiction where the site physically is.

locality.description: Sub-national location (city, region, park) exactly as a source gives it.

nameplate_it_capacity_mw.description: Nameplate IT capacity in megawatts: the IT load the facility is designed to serve (EN-04, TQ-10). Never interconnection capacity. not_applicable for sites that are not data centres.

technology.description: A vendor-neutral way of making, integrating, designing or delivering something. Not a thing that is shipped, and not a vendor's named offering.

broader.description: Broader technologies this one is a kind of. Empty means top level. Several parents are allowed (blur B-1: TSV). Taxonomy only: 'is part of' and 'requires' are S04 relationships.

definition.description: The Atlas working definition. Competing source definitions are preserved in the cited claims.

component.description: A vendor-neutral class of physical item: either built into AI compute hardware or used to make it. A class, never a vendor's named product.

broader.description: Broader component classes this one is a kind of (e.g. a data-centre GPU is a kind of AI accelerator). Empty means top level. Composition ('HBM base die is part of an HBM stack') is an S04 relationship, not this field.

definition.description: The Atlas working definition. Competing source definitions are preserved in the cited claims.

product.description: A specific commercial offering, named by the company that offers it: a chip, a memory product, a system, a software product or a service. An instance of a component or technology class.

vendor.description: The company that offers the product under this name. Part of the product's identity. Who designs, fabricates or packages it are S04 relationships.

instance_of.description: The vendor-neutral classes this product belongs to.

vendor_process_name.description: The fabrication process exactly as the vendor names it (FAB-05, TQ-07). Not comparable across vendors; no leading-edge threshold is derived from it.

tdp_w.description: Thermal design power of a chip or component, in watts, as the vendor states it (EN-03).

rated_power_w.description: Rated power of a server or system, in watts, as the manufacturer specifies it (EN-03).

rack_scale.description: Whether the vendor describes the system as a rack-scale design (DC-06).

cooling_method.description: Cooling method the vendor states for the system (DC-06).

jurisdiction.description: A territory with its own legal authority. The v1 kind is country only. The id slug is the ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code in lower case, so the code has one home.

display_name.description: The label the Atlas displays. An editorial choice, not a sourced fact; the sourced legal name is a separate field where it matters.

aliases.description: Other names under which sources refer to this record, used to detect duplicates. May be empty.

claim_ids.description: References to claim records (S06). The claim holds the source, locator, claim type and evidence status.

concept_refs.description: S01 domain-map concept IDs this record realises. Traceability from records back to the research. The concept prefix also gives the chain layer, so no layer field is stored.

partial_date.description: ISO 8601 calendar date at the precision the source gives: YYYY, YYYY-MM or YYYY-MM-DD.

assertion.description: One sourced value of an attribute. valid_from and valid_to bound the period the cited claims support; leave them out when the source gives no period.

unresolved.description: An explicit statement that no sourced value is recorded, and why (MA §5.7). A missing field or null is never accepted in its place.

attr_positive_number.description: Strictly positive: a zero is never used to mean unknown.

attr_boolean.description: false only when a source states the negative. Absence of a statement is not_researched, never false.

vocab_entity_type.description: Instantiable domain-entity types (D-022). Reserved types (institution, policy) and record kinds owned by other sessions (source, claim, event, relationship) are deliberately absent, so records of those kinds fail here.

vocab_actor_role.description: Business-model roles a company can hold (D-024). A role is claim-backed; it is never derived from missing relationships.

oneOf.description: Designs and sells chips, and buys wafer fabrication from a foundry operator and assembly, test and packaging from others.
Integrated device manufacturer: performs design, wafer fabrication, and assembly, test and packaging itself.
Operates fab capacity that makes chips designed by other firms (the foundry business model). An IDM that sells foundry services holds this role for those services (TQ-04).
Outsourced semiconductor assembly and test firm: performs assembly, test and packaging for third-party customers.
Fabricates DRAM and, in the v1 chain, stacks it into HBM supplied to the maker of the logic package.
Offers computing resources as a cloud service (the NIST cloud model) from facilities on its own premises. 'Hyperscaler' is not a separate role (TQ-08).
Makes and sells semiconductor manufacturing equipment: capital tools used to fabricate, assemble, test or package chips. Replaces MA §6.1 EquipmentSupplier (D-023).
Makes and sells electronic design automation tools.
A semiconductor fabrication facility where chips are made on wafers, logic or memory. The facility, not the business model: see actor role foundry_operator (TQ-04).
A facility where dies are assembled, packaged and tested, including 2.5D and 3D advanced packaging.
A facility used to house computer systems and associated components (LBNL). A cloud region or availability zone is not a facility (D-022).
A way of fabricating, patterning, stacking or packaging (e.g. TSV formation, 2.5D interposer integration, EUV lithography).
A way of architecting a chip or system that changes what must be manufactured (e.g. a multi-die accelerator).
A class of design or engineering software, independent of any vendor's product (e.g. EDA).
A way of delivering computing to users (e.g. cloud computing as NIST defines it).
Becomes physically part of AI compute hardware: a die, a memory stack, an accelerator, a server.
A tool used to make constituents and not built into them (semiconductor manufacturing equipment).
A physical product: a chip, a memory product, a server or system, a manufacturing tool.
A licensed software product, such as an EDA tool.
A service offering, such as a cloud compute service.

A state or territory with its own ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code. The code is used as an identifier; it states no position on sovereignty. Supranational jurisdictions are reserved for the EU lens (D-008, D-022).
The vendor states the system is liquid-cooled.
The vendor states the system is air-cooled.

vocab_unresolved_state.description: MA §5.7 states for a value that is not recorded. 'verified' and 'disputed' describe evidence, so they live on claims (S06), not here.

oneOf.description: No source has been checked for this value yet. Says nothing about whether the value is public.
Research found the value is not publicly disclosed. The cited claims show why.
The attribute does not apply to this record, e.g. nameplate IT capacity for a wafer fab.
